name: Anglesea

facts.claim: Anglesea is a Great Ocean Road town in the Surf Coast Shire about 110 km from Melbourne and 37 km from Geelong
Its main beach is home to the Anglesea Surf Life Saving Club and sits beside the tidal Anglesea River mouth
Eastern grey kangaroos live on the Anglesea golf course and can be seen from the road without a green fee
The river is used for fishing, paddleboarding and kayaking

name: Johanna Beach

facts.claim: Johanna Beach is an exposed ocean beach about 3.6 km long between Slippery Point and Rotten Point, with the Johanna River crossing its middle
It is a well-known surf break that hosted the 1970 World Surfing Championships and has been a backup venue for the Rip Curl Pro
The beach is unpatrolled and more exposed than other parts of the coast, and a basic campground sits behind it in Great Otway National Park
The beach is named for the brig Johanna, wrecked at the river mouth in 1843

name: Gibson Steps

facts.claim: Gibson Steps is a staircase of 86 steps cut into the cliffs down to Gibson Beach in Port Campbell National Park
It is the first stop in Port Campbell National Park for travellers heading west on the Great Ocean Road, about 2 minutes' drive from the Twelve Apostles
From the sand the cliffs rise above and the offshore stacks Gog and Magog stand just beyond the shore
The beach descent can close when tide and swell are unsafe

name: Mount Buninyong

facts.claim: Mount Buninyong is an extinct volcano rising to 745 m, 14 km south of Ballarat, inside the Mount Buninyong Scenic Reserve
A lookout tower at the summit gives 360-degree views, and walks include a Crater Walk with an accessible viewing platform, a zigzag Summit Walk and a South Walk
The forested reserve is a major koala habitat
In 1837 squatters viewed the future Ballarat district from its peak

name: Geelong Waterfront

facts.claim: Geelong Waterfront is a tourist and recreation area on the north-facing shore of Corio Bay, redeveloped in the 1990s from the former port
More than 100 painted timber bollards by artist Jan Mitchell run along the waterfront between Rippleside and Limeburners Point
The Carousel Pavilion houses a c.1892 Armitage-Herschell steam-driven carousel
Yarra Street Pier has restaurants, and the Geelong Flyer ferry runs from Steampacket Pier to Docklands

name: Mount Donna Buang

facts.claim: Mount Donna Buang is a 1,250 m mountain about 94 km from Melbourne, inside Yarra Ranges National Park, and the closest snowfield to Melbourne
In winter the summit gets snow for snowplay and tobogganing, and in other months it is visited by bushwalkers, cyclists and picnickers
A 21 m lookout tower at the summit has views over the Yarra Valley, Dandenong and Cathedral Ranges
The Mount Donna Buang Skywalk is a canopy walkway through myrtle beech and mountain ash at nearby Cement Creek
